learning_objective: 🎯 Step into 2D space! Learn how to add arrows (vectors), resolve forces, and master the beautiful curves of projectile and circular motion.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Scalars just have magnitude (like mass or temperature). Vectors have BOTH magnitude and a specific direction (like force or velocity). You cannot add vectors using normal math; you must use geometry!

We use the Triangle Law or Parallelogram Law to add vectors. 'Resolution' is breaking a vector into its X and Y components ($A_x = A\cos\theta$ and $A_y = A\sin\theta$). It makes 2D math incredibly easy!

Throw a ball in the air at an angle! The horizontal motion has zero acceleration (constant speed), while the vertical motion is controlled entirely by gravity. The resulting path (trajectory) is always a parabola.
Velocity depends on the observer. The velocity of object A relative to object B is $\mathbf{v}_{AB} = \mathbf{v}_A - \mathbf{v}_B$. This is used to solve 'Rain-Umbrella' and 'River-Boat' problems.

Moving in a circle at a constant speed. Even though the speed is constant, the direction is constantly changing, so the object is ALWAYS accelerating! This is called Centripetal Acceleration ($a_c = v^2/r$) directed towards the center.

fun_activity.title: 💦 The Hosepipe Angle
fun_activity.instructions: Take a garden hose and pinch the tip to make the water shoot far. Try different angles. You will notice the water travels the absolute furthest horizontal distance when you aim the nozzle exactly at a 45-degree angle!

exam_tips: 📌 For projectile motion, remember that the horizontal velocity component ($u\cos\theta$) NEVER changes throughout the flight (assuming no air resistance).
📌 Master the derivations for Maximum Height ($H$), Time of Flight ($T$), and Horizontal Range ($R$).
📌 In uniform circular motion, the velocity vector and acceleration vector are always exactly perpendicular ($90^\circ$) to each other.
quick_recap: ⭐ A unit vector (like $\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}$) has a magnitude of exactly 1 and is used purely to indicate direction.
⭐ The range of a projectile is the same for complementary angles (e.g., $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$).
⭐ Centripetal acceleration is what keeps planets orbiting the sun and cars turning on a curved road.
